depraved

dih-PRAYVD · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Depraved is morally corrupt; wicked or perverted.

The true-crime documentary described a depraved cult leader who manipulated his followers into giving up everything they owned.

Example

Courtroom testimony revealed just how depraved the con man was: his scheme had targeted elderly victims who trusted him completely.

The testimony showed a person acting with deep, deliberate wickedness toward vulnerable victims -- exactly the moral corruption depraved describes.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

corrupt: Corrupt means lacking moral principles -- willing to act wrongly, especially by abusing power for money or favors. Depraved goes much further: a depraved person is not just dishonest but deeply wicked, even enjoying cruelty. A corrupt official sells favors; a depraved one delights in the harm itself.

wicked: Wicked means morally very bad -- evil in what one intends or does. Depraved adds the sense of total moral rot: a depraved mind has lost its conscience so completely that cruelty feels normal. One wicked act can shock; depraved describes the whole ruined character behind such acts.

degenerate: Degenerate points at a fall: a person or thing that has sunk below a former, better standard. Depraved measures the depth of wickedness itself and says nothing about what came before. A once-proud club can grow degenerate; only real cruelty and moral rot earn the word depraved.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

virtuous: having high moral standards

upright: strictly honest and morally correct

Where it sits · how deep the moral rot goes — unscrupulous → depraved → monstrous

unscrupulous vs. depraved: Someone unscrupulous is willing to act dishonestly to get ahead, a lesser degree of moral failure than depraved.

monstrous vs. depraved: Monstrous behavior is so extreme it seems almost inhuman, an even more severe judgment than depraved.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: down, thoroughly (an intensifying use) (Latin)

Root — prav

Root — prav: crooked, perverse (from Latin pravus, 'crooked, perverse')

Suffix — -ed

Suffix — -ed: adjective-forming ending, 'made or marked by' (English)

Put it together

Put it together: Depraved combines de- ("thoroughly") with prav ("crooked, perverse," from Latin pravus) and the adjective ending -ed -- literally "thoroughly crooked." No everyday standalone English word survives from pravus alone, but its close relative depravity (the noun form of this same word) is still common.

Use the root in a new word: depravity

Use the root in a new word: depravity: The court records describe the full depravity of his crimes in disturbing detail.

Word Building

Word Choice

Depraved is a strong word for deep moral corruption or wickedness -- stronger than debased, which more often describes something reduced in quality or value rather than actively evil.
